summary: A dense worker-placement euro where the strength of your dice-workers determines which action spaces you can claim, forcing constant tradeoffs between speed and power across resource gathering, card acquisition, and church-track advancement. Games reward building an efficient engine of development cards that snowball into strong late-round turns.
praised: deep, satisfying engine-building with many viable strategies
clever dice-as-workers mechanism that adds tactical texture to placement
excellent production and long-term replayability, especially with the included expansions
strong sense of progression as your tableau compounds
criticised: steep learning curve and heavy rulebook for newcomers
dice/card luck can swing available options
prone to analysis paralysis in the mid-to-late game

interaction.kind: worker placement with dice, indirect blocking
interaction.detail: Players compete for a limited set of shared action spaces and cards, so claiming a strong spot or card denies it to everyone else, but each player otherwise develops their own private board of resources, cards, and tracks. The shared council/church track and excommunication penalties are the main points of direct cross-player effect.

scoring.why: Final score adds VP printed on development, territory, character, and building cards to military-track position, faith bonuses, and leftover resources converted at game end.
scoring.how_you_win: Across six rounds, place family members (boosted by dice values) to collect resources and acquire cards from four decks, then total all card VP, track bonuses, and end-game conversions; the highest sum wins.
